items.title: Ghana’s tomato, ginger shortfalls deepen import bill, CSIR researchers say
items.description: Ghana’s tomato imports alone exceed US$230 million annually, while a disease-driven collapse of ginger has left the country 99 per cent import-dependent, Council for Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) researchers have said, urging a research-led recovery. Scientists at CSIR said the country’s increasing dependence on imports highlights weak seed systems, limited irrigation, poor soil health, disease pressure, and insufficient investment in horticultural research. They were speaking at the second session of the 2026 Ministry of Environment, Science, Technology and Innovation (MEST) Visibility Webinar Series, held virtually on the theme “CSIR’s Interventions on Tomato and Ginger”. Dr Michael Kwabena Osei, Principal Research Scientist and vegetable breeder at the CSIR Crop Research Institute, reported that national demand for fresh and processed tomatoes now exceeded 1.4 million metric tonnes annually, but local production met only about 15 to 18 per cent of that requirement. He explained that Ghana produced about 120,000 to 180,000 metric tonnes of tomato a year from an estimated 25,000 to 30,000 hectares, leaving an annual supply deficit of about 1.1 million metric tonnes. Fresh tomato imports, mainly from Burkina Faso, were estimated at 100,000 to 120,000 metric tonnes annually, costing about US$18 million, while processed tomato imports, largely from China and Europe, were equivalent to 400,000 to 450,000 metric tonnes of raw tomato and cost about US$150 million. Dr Osei stated that combined tomato imports exceeded US$230 million a year yet still filled only about 40 per cent of the country’s tomato shortfall. More than 60 per cent of fresh tomato imports enter Ghana during the dry season, between November and April, when local supply falls sharply, he said. Despite having more than 400,000 hectares of arable land suitable for tomato cultivation, Ghana’s average yield remains between seven and 10 tonnes per hectare, compared with potential yields of 20 to 80 tonnes under improved varieties and good agronomic management. Dr Osei said the constraint was not land but technology, citing quality seed, plant protection, dry-season water, healthy soils and sound agronomy as the missing links. “A country that imports its seed will always import its food,” he said. He noted that about 89 per cent of tomato farmers were small-scale growers cultivating between five and 20 acres, while many relied on seed extracted from ripe fruit or recycled hybrids that lost vigour and productivity. More than 85 per cent of tomato seed planted in Ghana was expensive commercial hybrid seed, he said, calling for a stronger domestic seed system to reduce dependence on imports. Dr Osei also pointed to irrigation gaps, saying only about 9,000 hectares of the 15,000 hectares covered by 22 public irrigation schemes were currently in use. He said public irrigation schemes and affordable dry-season water were central to reducing imports, especially as crops could fail when temperatures rose above 32 degrees Celsius. The tomato sector was also being held back by weak extension support, acidic soils, bacterial wilt, nematodes, low organic matter and a struggling processing industry, he added. Dr Osei said the state-owned Pwalugu Tomato Factory, established in 1961 with a capacity of 500 tonnes a day, had been non-functional for years, while private processors relied largely on imported concentrate instead of local fruit. He stated that the CSIR had already released two open-pollinated tomato varieties, CRI-Kwabena Kwabena and CRI-Copia, which have shelf lives of approximately 18 and 21 days, respectively, and that it holds the largest tomato germplasm in Ghana. The researchers proposed a range of interventions spanning short-, medium- and long-term strategies. These include the rapid evaluation of existing crop varieties, the production of certified seeds, training programmes for farmers, the establishment of solar powered boreholes, improvements in soil quality, the creation of mechanisation hubs, and the implementation of protected cultivation techniques Dr Osei said Ghana also needed a Tomato Board by 2028 and a dedicated Horticultural Research Institute by 2030 to coordinate research, seed development, processing, financing and market integration. He summarised the proposed recovery framework as “policy to protect, research to solve, and market to make profit.” On ginger, Dr Osei noted that national demand had risen from about 18,000 tonnes in 2020 to between 30,000 and 32,000 tonnes in 2025, but production collapsed after a bacterial wilt outbreak in 2022. The disease, caused by Ralstonia solanacearum and locally referred to as the “ginger killer”, reduced national production from about 102 tonnes to roughly 10 tonnes, leaving Ghana more than 99 percent dependent on imported ginger. Ghana now spent about US$500,000 annually importing ginger, mainly from China, Nigeria and Burkina Faso, he added. The supply shock had driven prices sharply upward, with a sack of ginger rising from about GH¢250 in 2022 to GH¢4,000 in 2025 and about GH¢6,000 or more at the time of the webinar. Dr Osei noted that the disease was soil-borne, spread through infected planting material, poor drainage, heavy rains, monocropping and contaminated farm tools, and could not be chemically treated once a crop was infected. He stated that CSIR’s recovery plan for ginger rested on four pillars: development of resistant varieties, production of disease-free planting material through tissue culture, disease surveillance and integrated pest management, and farmer deployment through extension networks. Ms Matilda Frimpong, a ginger research scientist at CSIR-CRI, advised that growers should obtain certified rhizomes from certified companies or research institutions because the wilt pathogen was microscopic, soil-borne and could not be identified by sight. She noted that the most sustainable long-term control measure was breeding for resistance, beyond crop rotation and other cultural practices. Dr Richard Yaw Agyare, vegetable breeder at the CSIR Savannah Agricultural Research Institute, indicated that northern Ghana, particularly the Upper East Region, once played a leading role in national tomato production but many irrigation sites now produced little tomato. He said national tomato output had stagnated at about 360,000 tonnes annually for nearly a decade, with productivity around 7.8 tonnes per hectare, far below Morocco’s 94 tonnes and Burkina Faso’s 17 tonnes per hectare. Dr Agyare attributed the northern production decline to pests and diseases, declining soil fertility, weak agronomy, recycled hybrid seed, heat stress, poor market incentives and competition from imported Burkina Faso tomatoes. He said heat stress from February onwards shortened the dry-season production window, while the absence of rainy-season varieties suited to hot, humid conditions limited year-round production. The SARI, he stated, was breeding tomato varieties for both rainfed and dry-season ecologies, with promising lines undergoing validation and multi-location trials. He added that adding climate-smart varieties could increase yields, improve fruit quality, raise farmer incomes, support nutrition, revive processing industries and reduce Ghana’s tomato import bill. Rev. Dr Cephas Adjei Mensah, the Director of Research, Statistics and Information Management at MEST, said that the government was encouraged by CSIR’s interventions and would follow up on proposals for stronger institutional support. He welcomed the call for a dedicated horticultural research institute, saying it could be framed as a centre of excellence to serve Ghana, West Africa and the wider continent. The webinar was moderated by Prof. Maxwell D. Asante, Director of CSIR-CRI, and formed part of MEST’s visibility series to showcase research interventions supporting national development.

items.title: Pakistan warns UN Security Council of ‘tipping point’ in occupied West Bank
items.description: • Calls on international community to pressure Israel to halt settlement expansion on Palestinian land • Guterres says Israeli settlements in occupied West Bank have no legal validity and violate international law WASHINGTON: Pakistan on Tuesday urged the international community to persuade Israel to halt new Jewish settlements on Palestinian lands, warning that the situation was approaching a “dangerous tipping point”, as UN Secretary-General António Guterres said all Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank had no legal validity and constituted a “flagrant violation” of international law. Britain urged Israel to do more to prevent and prosecute settler violence, while Russia warned that the West Bank was approaching a “point of no return” and risked profound regional destabilisation, as the UN Security Council debated escalating attacks on Palestinians and settlement expansion. “The situation is approaching a dangerous tipping point. Unless this trajectory is reversed, the consequences for the two-state solution — and for peace and stability across the region — could be catastrophic,” Pakistan’s UN Ambassador Asim Iftikhar Ahmad told the Council. He told the Security Council that settlement expansion, settler violence, land seizures and the extension of Israeli authority over Palestinian land were part of a broader effort to entrench the occupation and undermine the prospects of a Palestinian state. He said these measures were fragmenting Palestinian territory and, together with settler violence, had produced the largest displacement crisis in occupied West Bank since 1967. Pakistan also expressed alarm over escalating provocations at Al Aqsa Mosque, calling on Israel to respect the historical and legal status quo at the holy sites and halt provocative actions. Ahmad called for international protection for Palestinians and accountability for those responsible for settler violence. He also urged Israel to immediately release Palestinian tax revenues it was withholding, saying the money belonged to the Palestinian people and that its continued withholding was severely undermining Palestinian institutions. British Ambassador Sarah MacIntosh condemned escalating violence across the occupied West Bank, describing attacks by Israeli settlers on Palestinian villages and communities, sometimes alongside Israeli Defence Forces, as “appalling”. She said children were being exposed to repeated violence, displacement and disruption, citing the August 4 demolition by Israeli forces of three donor-funded classrooms at Shaab al-Butum school. MacIntosh said Israeli settlers had acted with impunity for too long. “Much more must be done to prevent and prosecute acts of violence,” she said. She also called for a halt to settlement expansion, saying the settlements were illegal under international law and undermined the viability of a two-state solution. Russian Ambassador Vassily A. Nebenzia said the West Bank was “approaching a point of no return”, warning of the risk of profound regional destabilisation. He blamed Israel for its “creeping” settlement expansion, escalating violence and an “unprecedented” tightening of movement restrictions on Palestinians. Nebenzia said Israel continued its “illegal policy of building new settlements”, pointing to a government tender issued last week for more than 600 housing units in Ramallah al-Bireh. The UN relief agency OCHA reported that 1,122 Palestinians were killed in the occupied West Bank between Oct 7, 2023, when the Gaza conflict began, and July 24, 2026. The toll included 76 Palestinians killed this year. OCHA said Israeli forces or settlers injured at least 37 Palestinians between July 28 and August 3, while 35 settler attacks were documented during the same period. The UN human rights office said last month that settler violence had reached an “all-time high” as new settlements were approved. It said Israeli settlers and Israeli security forces had “often” acted together in attacks on Palestinian communities. Pakistan said the cumulative effect of settlement expansion, settler violence, land seizures and other measures was intimidation, dispossession and forced displacement. “The path to peace lies in ending the Israeli occupation and enabling the Palestinian people to exercise their inalienable right to self-determination,” Ahmad said, calling for an independent, sovereign, viable and contiguous Pale­stinian state based on the pre-1967 borders, with Al Quds Al Sharif as its capital. Published in Dawn, August 12th, 2026

items.title: Mideast outreach
items.description: OVER the past few days, Pakistan has been going the extra mile to assure Iran that the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement it signed last week with Saudi Arabia and Turkiye poses no threat to Tehran. In a recent telephone call, Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar told his Iranian counterpart Abbas Araghchi that the pact is “not an instrument of confrontation”. Moreover, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif told the cabinet that the agreement is “entirely for defence purposes”. Tehran seems to have understood the messaging, as the Iranian foreign ministry spokesman said his country had no reason to believe the pact was aimed at encircling it, and that it showed that countries of the region could not depend on the American security umbrella. Perhaps the reason for speculation surrounding the deal was the mutual defence component, which says that an attack on one signatory is an attack on all. Considering the targeting of US military assets in Saudi Arabia and other Gulf states by Iran during the active phase of hostilities with America, observers have debated whether the signatories of the deal could step in militarily. However, the clarifications regarding Iran are welcome. In fact, what is needed is a new regional security architecture that binds the Arabs, Iranians and other states together. Achieving this would be difficult, considering the pro-America stance of the GCC states. However, the American military footprint in the Gulf and larger Middle East may eventually shrink, which means that regional states will have to eventually work out a security framework amongst themselves. The Makkah pact could provide a blueprint for such defence cooperation. The Turkish president has already said that the pact is open to other countries. If Iran were to be brought on board, it could significantly alter the regional security landscape. For this to happen, the existing high levels of mistrust between the Arabs, particularly Saudi Arabia, and the Iranians, would need to be reduced. But states such as Pakistan and Turkiye, which maintain cordial ties with both sides, can attempt to bridge the gap. As a CBM, Iran should open up the Strait of Hormuz, as its continued closure is battering Gulf economies. The Arab states should also pledge to disallow outsiders from staging aggression against Iran from their soil. Instead of depending on extra-regional powers, the states of the Gulf and Middle East must themselves create a new security architecture. Not only would this reduce the tensions that exist between them, it could also serve as an expanded defence pact to deter Israel from attacking regional states. Tel Aviv has attacked Iran and its allies, as well as pro-America states like Qatar, hence an effective regional defensive bloc could make Israel think twice about its violent adventurism. Published in Dawn, August 12th, 2026

items.title: Beyond connectivity, Telecel Group is investing in young learners’ digital and soft skills
items.description: Before Dorcas first joined the Skills for School Programme, she barely spoke in class. She was shy, struggled with anxiety and often doubted herself. Standing up in class to answer a simple question felt difficult. “The first time I answered a question during one of the training sessions, I felt proud of myself. The Skills for School programme helped me to speak up, work with others, set goals and believe that I could become a leader,” Dorcas recalled. Today, Dorcas reflects on a very different story. She served as Girls’ Prefect in her final year of junior high, rose to become Sub-Commander of her school’s Cadet Team, built a study group that grew from 8 to 32 students, and discovered the confidence to pursue her career dream of joining the military. The Skills for School programme, delivered by King’s Trust International in partnership with Junior Achievement Ghana, has supported more than 5,000 young people since its launch in 2020. Working with 11 to 17-year-olds across 31 schools in the Greater Accra Region, the programme focuses on young people who may be disengaged from learning or experiencing challenges with confidence, communication and self-management. Through the programme, participants develop the core skills needed to succeed in education, employment and life. Through the partnership with Telecel Group, the programme has expanded its impact by introducing a significant digital learning component. The funding has helped improve access to essential technology and infrastructure, including the establishment of computer laboratories in seven schools within the Accra Metropolitan, Krowor and Kpone Katamanso municipalities of the Greater Accra Region. Telecel Group’s support has also enabled the development of a new digital safety module, which is now being delivered to students across all 31 participating schools. During a recent visit to observe the sessions first-hand in one of the partner schools, executives from Telecel Ghana interacted with students whose lives are being transformed by the training. External Affairs Director of Telecel Ghana, Komla Buami, said the telecommunications multinational recognises that the digital future depends on preparing young people with the skills needed to thrive in an increasingly digital world. “Telecel Group’s investment is about giving young people the confidence to speak up, solve problems, collaborate with others and use technology as a tool to create opportunities. “These are the skills that are in demand in the workplace. We are pleased to see the impact the sessions are having on students’ digital and soft skills development.” Programme Manager at Junior Achievement Ghana, Lorretta Domfeh Owusu, said the initiative targets young people who face challenges with confidence, communication, self-management and academic engagement, including learners with disabilities. “Our partnership with Telecel Group has significantly enhanced the programme. The computers and internet access provided have enabled students to build digital skills and safely navigate the online space through our digital safeguarding module. “They are also using tools like Microsoft Copilot to create vision boards for their goal setting, making learning more engaging and practical.” Andre Harriman, Head of Delivery for Africa at King’s Trust International, highlighted the importance of cross-sector partnerships in equipping young people with the skills and tools needed to succeed in an increasingly digital world. “We are delighted that Telecel Group is supporting our work with Junior Achievement Ghana to address the critical core skills and digital infrastructure needs of young people in Ghana. “This partnership has enabled us to introduce a new digital dimension to the Skills for School programme, helping students develop practical digital skills and an understanding of online safety that will support both their educational journeys and future livelihoods,” Mr. Harriman said.

items.title: Here’s why Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8 is perfect device for your favourite content
items.description: From streaming and gaming to reading and discovering new content, the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8 brings an expansive foldable display and intelligent Galaxy AI experiences to the content people enjoy every day. Currently available for pre-order in Ghana, Galaxy Z Fold8 combines the portability of a smartphone with an immersive, tablet-like viewing experience. As the global leader in foldables, Samsung’s innovations have moved the category forward year after year, creating the thin, light and durable designs, innovative AI experiences and stunning displays that users love. Galaxy Z Fold8, unveiled alongside the latest Galaxy Z series line-up at Galaxy Unpacked on July 22, continues that legacy of innovation. Its display features all-new Flex Titanium technology to make the device thin without compromising durability. The new display also creates a less visible crease for immersive viewing anytime, anywhere. How is Galaxy Z Fold8 different from other Galaxy Z series foldables? items.title: UAE donates relief items worth over GH¢12m to June 29 flood victims
items.description: The United Arab Emirates (UAE) has donated relief items valued at more than GH₵12 million to support communities and families affected by the June 29 floods in Ghana. The donation, comprising food, rice, drinking water, blankets and sleeping mattresses, was formally presented at the headquarters of the National Disaster Management Organisation (NADMO) in Accra. A symbolic presentation of the items was subsequently made to some flood-affected victims within the Circle enclave, as part of efforts to demonstrate the immediate reach of the humanitarian assistance. At the NADMO warehouse, the relief items were being packaged for onward distribution to flood-affected communities and families. The assistance includes 13,000 food boxes, 20,000 rice packages, each containing approximately two to three kilogrammes of rice, 10,000 cartons of bottled water, with 30 bottles per carton, more than 8,000 blankets and more than 5,000 sleeping mattresses. The relief items were all procured in Ghana, supporting local businesses and boosting the Ghanaian economy. The donation follows the Government’s appeal for international support to assist victims of the June 29 floods, which displaced nearly 90,000 people, affected close to 80,000 households and claimed about 34 lives. The UAE intervention was informed by a Rapid Needs Assessment conducted with NADMO and humanitarian partners, which identified food assistance as the highest priority for 93 per cent of affected communities. Blankets, mattresses and safe drinking water were also identified among the urgent needs. The relief effort forms part of the broader Ghana-UAE partnership and is intended to support the Government’s response to communities affected by the floods and assist affected families with essential relief items. Mr Seidu Issifu, Minister of State for Climate Change and Sustainability at the Office of the President, said the President, Mr John Dramani Mahama, had approved the Climate Emergency Resource Mobilisation Track to mobilise international partnerships for immediate relief, recovery and long-term climate resilience. “Today, we witness the tangible impact of that vision,” he said, and described the UAE’s response as a remarkable demonstration of the enduring friendship between Ghana and the UAE. He noted that the country had supported Ghana through investments, development operations and humanitarian assistance. Mr Issifu expressed gratitude to the UAE Ambassador to Ghana, Dr Abdulla Al Mandoos, the UAE Aid Agency and other officials for responding to Ghana’s appeal within a short period. He also commended the Ministries of Foreign Affairs and Interior, NADMO and other government departments and agencies for coordinating the intervention. “This partnership exemplifies the whole-of-government approach required to respond effectively to climate emergencies,” he said. Mr Issifu assured the UAE Government and people that the donation would be put to its intended use and reach the communities and families most affected by the floods. He also called on other international partners and agencies that had received Ghana’s appeal to support the country, saying climate change could not be addressed by one country alone. “Climate change cannot be fought by one person. It needs our collaborative efforts to be able to navigate through the crisis,” he said. Mr Rashid Salem Al Shamsi, Executive Director of Operations at the UAE Aid Agency, said the UAE believed that helping others in times of need was based on unity, cooperation and shared responsibility. He said the UAE stood with Ghana and supported the national efforts to assist people affected by the floods and facilitate their recovery. “We stand with Ghana and support your national efforts to help those affected and to assist recovery,” he said, adding that the friendship between the two countries continued to grow. The UAE official expressed sympathy to families affected by the floods and wished them a speedy recovery. Dr Abdulla Al Mandoos, Ambassador of the United Arab Emirates to Ghana, said the UAE was committed to supporting Ghanaian communities affected by the floods. “The true strength of any partnership is revealed in moments of hardship. The United Arab Emirates is proud to stand alongside Ghana, not only as a friend, but as a trusted partner committed to supporting its people during times of difficulty. We hope these essential supplies bring relief and reassurance to affected families as they continue their journey towards recovery,” he said. Mr Ebenezer Okletey Terlabi, Deputy Minister for the Interior, described the donation as a generous gesture of friendship at a time when countries across the world continued to face the devastating effects of natural and human-induced disasters. He said humanitarian assistance was not simply about the relief items but also about restoring hope and dignity to people affected by unfortunate circumstances. “Every item that reaches a vulnerable family represents a message that they are not alone and that the international community cares about their well-being,” he said. Mr Terlabi said the Government and NADMO would ensure that the relief items were properly managed and delivered to the people and communities that needed them most. Mr James Gyakyi Quayson, Deputy Minister for Foreign Affairs, expressed appreciation to the UAE Government and people for the humanitarian assistance. He said the gesture deepened the enduring friendship between Ghana and the UAE and would inspire greater cooperation between the two countries.

items.title: Murad vows action over police, medico-legal lapses as Mir Raza murder probe progresses
items.description: • Says proposed judicial commission meant to identify lapses, not for murder investigation • Two more police officials added to investigation team • Four summoned by NCCIA on Sharjeel’s plea against online defamation campaign KARACHI: As the probe into the murder of a young businessman inches forward, Sindh Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah has assured the family of a fair investigation, promising that they will be kept informed at every stage of the process. Talking to the media at the Arts Council Karachi after attending a conference held in connection with National Minorities Day on Tuesday evening, the CM said action would be taken against police and medico-legal authorities over any lapses once the case was resolved. Commenting on the provincial government’s plan to form a judicial commission , the CM clarified that the commission was not intended to investigate the case, as that was the responsibility of the police. “The judicial commission was being formed to identify lapses on the part of the police and medico-legal authorities,” he said. Mr Shah said he had sent the home minister and the Karachi mayor to meet Mir Raza’s parents before the announcement about the commission, and the family had agreed to its formation. “However, when the family later said they did not want a judicial commission, we respected their opinion,” he added. ‘Traces of acid found on deceased’s shirt’ Investigators probing the murder case received the chemical analysis report from the first post-mortem examination that confirmed traces of acid on the shirt of the deceased. Informed sources told Dawn that the report also confirmed the presence of “gunshot residue on the back of the perforation of the shirt,” which was the entry wound. The sources said that several samples were collected during the second post-mortem examination following the exhumation of the body and so far, only the report of a DNA test had been received that confirmed that the body was of Mir Raza. Meanwhile, the sources said that the investigators also decided to conduct geofencing of different parts of the area surrounding the crime scene in Gulistan-i-Jauhar to detect the possible movements people during a particular time. Besides this, the call data records of the victim’s cell phone would also be obtained. The sources said that, at the request of family’s lawyer Jibran Nasir, two new members — DSP Siraj Lashari and Inspector Mohammed Ali —had been included in the investigation team headed by DIG Amir Farooqui. Mir Raza, an IBA graduate and owner of the eatery Wafflix, had gone missing on July 28, and his body was found a day later in bushes near Shahi Qila Ground in Gulistan-i-Jauhar. NCCIA summons four on Sharjeel’s plea The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) has summoned four citizens on a complaint filed by Sindh Senior Minister Sharjeel Inam Memon over “false and malicious content on social media against him and his son” in connection with the Mir Raza Ali murder case. The NCCIA issued notices to Syed Abdullah, Amin Qureshi, Bilal Warsi and Obaid Qureshi, asking them to appear in person at the agency’s Karachi office on Aug 13 at 11:30am. They were informed that the NCCIA was conducting an inquiry initiated on the basis of a complaint submitted by Naqvi Law Associates on behalf of Sharjeel Inam Memon pertaining to alleged dissemination of defamatory and fabricated content through digital platforms. The development comes a day after Mr Memon had approached the NCCIA against a defamatory campaign that he owned the guest house in Gulistan-i-Jauhar where Mir Raza Ali was allegedly tortured and murdered, and that his son had left for London immediately after the incident and had since been moving around with a bodyguard. Published in Dawn, August 12th, 2026

items.title: Govt cuts petrol price by Rs1.70, raises high-speed diesel by Rs1.39
items.description: Pakistan fuel prices, 2026 Official ex-depot prices (PKR/litre) — OGRA & Ministry of Energy notifications Petrol (MS-92) Diesel (HSD) Pre-crisis baseline Source: OGRA / Ministry of Energy (Petroleum Division); Dawn.com · "> The government on Tuesday reduced the price of petrol by Rs1.70 and increased the price of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs1.39 per litre. Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs325.92 per litre while HSD will cost Rs382.25 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on HSD. According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices will be applicable for August 12 (Wednesday). The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28. The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March. Earlier, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US. The government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel. The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends. The daily pricing decision was rejected by the All Pakistan Dealers Association, which said it would consider a protest plan. Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes. Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators. Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

items.title: Ghana strengthens fight against sea crimes with major Maritime Offences Bill
items.description: Ghana is strengthening its legal framework to combat piracy, armed robbery at sea, trafficking and other maritime-related crimes with the implementation of the Maritime and Related Offences Bill, 2026. The Bill, which has been passed by Parliament and is awaiting Presidential assent, seeks to provide a comprehensive legal regime for the prevention, investigation, prosecution and punishment of piracy, armed robbery at sea and other maritime offences. It also seeks to align Ghana’s laws with key provisions of the 1982 United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) and the 1988 Convention for the Suppression of Unlawful Acts Against the Safety of Maritime Navigation and its related protocols. The Ghana Maritime Authority (GMA), in collaboration with the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) and the European Union (EU), is, therefore, engaging key stakeholders to build a common understanding of the legislation ahead of its implementation. The engagement formed part of a two-day Stakeholder Sensitisation Workshop on the Maritime and Related Offences Bill, 2026, which opened in Accra on Wednesday, August 5. It was under the theme: “Enhancing Maritime Security in Africa: Safe Seas for Africa.” The workshop brought together officials from the Ministry of Transport, GMA, Ghana Navy, Ghana Air Force, Marine Police, Attorney-General’s Department and other institutions within the criminal justice system. Mr William Kartey, Chief Director of the Ministry of Transport, who delivered a welcome address on behalf of the Minister, said the Ministry was taking steps to position Ghana as a maritime hub in the sub-region. He said achieving that objective required legislation that was aligned with international legal frameworks governing maritime activities. Mr Kartey commended the EU, UNODC and GMA for supporting the stakeholder engagement, saying effective implementation of the legislation would require collaboration among the institutions responsible for maritime security and justice. For his part, Mr Mubarick Masawudu, Deputy Director-General of the GMA, said the maritime sector remained a vital pillar of Ghana’s economy but was increasingly exposed to sophisticated forms of maritime crime. He cited piracy, armed robbery at sea, trafficking and other forms of transnational organised crime as threats requiring a coordinated and effective response. “The Bill represents a significant milestone in Ghana’s efforts to strengthen its legal and institutional framework for combating maritime crime,” he said. Mr Masawudu said a robust legal framework was essential for effective investigations, successful prosecutions and coordinated law enforcement. He said the legislation would provide greater clarity and certainty and equip the relevant institutions with modern legal tools to suppress maritime crime. Although the Bill was awaiting Presidential assent, he noted that early engagement with stakeholders was necessary to ensure that the institutions responsible for its enforcement were adequately prepared. Mr Jean-Pierre Bardoul, Programme Officer, Governance Section of the EU, said maritime law enforcement agencies in the Gulf of Guinea were being supported through the Safe Seas for Africa project, implemented with the assistance of the EU and UNODC. The project, he said, sought to strengthen the capacity of maritime law enforcement agencies to prevent, investigate and prosecute piracy and other maritime crimes, including drug trafficking. Mr Bardoul said the Bill provided for alignment with important provisions of UNCLOS and would strengthen Ghana’s legal framework for addressing maritime crimes. He said the alignment would provide local courts with clearer jurisdiction and help address some of the prosecutorial challenges associated with maritime offences. Professor Martha Chantel Ribero, representing the UNODC, described the workshop as another milestone in the organisation’s engagement with Ghana’s criminal justice system. She said the UNODC was providing technical support for Ghana’s legal reform efforts through the Safe Seas for Africa project. Prof Ribero said the country’s efforts to strengthen its maritime legal framework were a positive step towards addressing maritime crime and enhancing the rule of law. The workshop examined measures to criminalise and deter maritime crime, deepen understanding of the international and regional legal frameworks underpinning the Bill, and considered the requirements for safe and secure shipping to support national economic development. “On our part at the UNODC, we remain committed to further supporting Ghana’s criminal justice sector in strengthening the rule of law through improved legislation, with the overall aim of tackling maritime crime,” Prof Ribero said. The stakeholder engagement is expected to enhance institutional understanding of the new legislation and strengthen coordination among agencies involved in Ghana’s maritime security and criminal justice systems. In addressing the legal gaps, Parliament’s Roads and Transportation Committee, in its report on the Bill, had noted that the absence of a dedicated legal framework on maritime offences had created enforcement and prosecutorial challenges in dealing with piracy and related crimes. The Committee said the legislation would provide the necessary legal basis for the investigation, arrest, prosecution and punishment of offenders. The parliamentary report also noted that the Gulf of Guinea had experienced increasing maritime insecurity, including vessel hijackings, kidnappings for ransom, armed robbery at sea and destruction of maritime property. It said such crimes posed significant threats to maritime trade, regional stability, economic development and the safety of seafarers. These necessitated stronger legal and institutional framework. Parliament also considered the legislation important to Ghana’s ambition of becoming a maritime hub in the sub-region, with the Committee noting that closing gaps in maritime law would strengthen trade security and enhance port control. The Bill was laid in Parliament on March 16, 2026, by Mr Joseph Bukari Nikpe, Minister for Transport.

items.title: France : plus de 1 800 livraisons de stupéfiants par drone vers une prison, cinq interpellations
items.description: Un vaste trafic de stupéfiants organisé à l’aide de drones a été démantelé près de la prison de Villefranche-sur-Saône. En seulement 51 jours, les enquêteurs ont recensé 1 826 livraisons. Cinq suspects ont été interpellés. Les gendarmes ont démantelé un réseau particulièrement organisé de livraisons de stupéfiants par drone à destination de la prison de Villefranche-sur-Saône, dans le centre-est de la France. Cinq personnes ont été interpellées dans le cadre de l’enquête. Le réseau aurait effectué 1 826 livraisons en 51 jours, depuis deux zones de décollage situées à proximité immédiate de l’établissement pénitentiaire. Trois suspects ont été arrêtés en flagrant délit. Parmi les cinq personnes interpellées figure un mineur, qui sera jugé en septembre et a été placé dans un centre éducatif fermé. Les quatre adultes doivent comparaître en octobre, dont trois sont actuellement en détention provisoire. Au cours des investigations, les enquêteurs ont notamment saisi 500 grammes de cannabis, 6 000 euros en liquide, un véhicule ainsi que le drone utilisé pour les livraisons. L’appareil était accompagné de 18 batteries, permettant d'assurer les nombreux vols. Les livraisons étaient principalement effectuées de nuit, avec des drones dépourvus de lumières afin de rendre leur localisation plus difficile. Une source syndicale pénitentiaire a souligné les difficultés rencontrées par les agents face à ce phénomène. « On entend le drone mais on ne sait pas où il est, ni à quelle cellule il livre », a-t-elle expliqué à l’AFP. Le recours aux drones pour approvisionner les prisons françaises semble prendre de l’ampleur. En 2025, environ 5 000 survols ou tentatives de survol de prisons avaient été recensés en France, contre un peu plus de 800 en 2024. Cette forte hausse est notamment liée au déploiement progressif de systèmes de détection des drones dans les établissements pénitentiaires. Les syndicats alertent également sur le risque d’une évolution de ces trafics. Après les stupéfiants, ils craignent notamment que les drones puissent être utilisés pour acheminer des armes ou d’autres objets dangereux dans les prisons. En janvier dernier, un ancien détenu de 26 ans avait déjà été condamné à six ans de prison ferme pour avoir dirigé un réseau de livraisons par drone destiné à des prisonniers dans le nord de la France. Dans cette affaire, les commandes étaient notamment passées via Snapchat et le réseau avait généré plus de deux millions d’euros de chiffre d’affaires. The post France : plus de 1 800 livraisons de stupéfiants par drone vers une prison, cinq interpellations appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Petroleum dealers issue 72-hour ultimatum
items.description: KARACHI: Pakistan Petroleum Dealers Associa­tion (PPDA) has issued a 72-hour ultimatum to the government over its failure to fulfil promises made by the petroleum minister to resolve their issues, especially the increase in margin to eight per cent on the retail sale price of petrol. The association warned that if the government failed to meet its demands within 72 hours, petrol pumps across the country would shut down indefinitely from 6am on Saturday (August 15) and would not reopen until those demands were met. PPDA Chairman Malik Khuda Bakhsh, along with senior office-bearers, told a press conference that petroleum dealers would be unable to continue their businesses if the government failed to accept their demands. Mr Malik said that, following a meeting of dealers from across the country, it had been jointly decided to demand an 8pc margin on petrol. Dealers’ patience had run out, and more than 14,000 members were putting pressure on the association to take action. Threaten indefinite nationwide shutdown from Aug 15 On Aug 7, the PPDA chairman informed the Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik that he had been receiving significant concerns from petroleum dealers and association members regarding the unresolved issues facing the petroleum retail sector. He recalled that when the association was considering a nationwide strike previously, the minister had requested the PPDA to defer the proposed action and assured us that the issues would be reviewed and reconciled within two weeks. The daily price mechanism system had created serious operational and financial challenges for the petroleum dealers, resulting in inventory losses, erosion of working capital and substantial financial strain on the retail sector, he informed the federal minister. The existing commission was insufficient to cover rising inflation, electricity and gas expenses, employees’ salaries and other operational costs, he said. Earlier, the PPDA Executive Committee meeting had also strongly criticised the “Company Allocation Policy,” describing it as discriminatory and contrary to the business interests of dealers. The association demanded that the policy be reviewed immediately and made transparent and fair. Published in Dawn, August 12th, 2026

items.title: UN chief expresses solidarity with quake-hit Colombia
items.description: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres on Tuesday expressed solidarity with Colombia, which was hit by a magnitude-7.5 earthquake on Monday, and extended his condolences to the families of the victims. In a post on X, Guterres wished all those affected a speedy recovery, as reports continued to emerge of collapsed homes and other significant damage. "The UN is in close contact with the Colombian authorities and is supporting the government-led response as requested," he added. The death toll from the earthquake in western Colombia has risen to 188, with 1,677 others injured, the Colombian Association of Capital Cities, or Asocapitales, said Tuesday. Asocapitales said it has launched a system to report and search for missing persons as rescue work and damage assessment continues. The quake tore through the country's coffee-growing heartland, leaving apartment blocks, homes, schools and health centers cracked, leaning or flattened. Thousands of people were left homeless as the earthquake brought down apartment complexes and left deep cracks in homes. Reuters reported that rescue crews on Tuesday dug through mountains of rubble in western Colombia, shouting for quiet so they could ‌listen for survivors still trapped. On Tuesday afternoon, three airports remained closed and many areas, especially those close to the epicenter, still lacked access to gas, water and electricity, while some major highways remained closed off. With communications still patchy in some of the worst-hit areas, government officials said it could take days to ascertain the full extent of the damage and the final death toll. The government, which ‌announced immediate austerity measures as it came into power, is currently preparing to revise a more than $180 billion budget. The National Coffee Federation was working on the ground with families to assess damage to farms and rural infrastructure, its chief German Bahamon said on social media. (With input from agencies)

items.description: Le coordonnateur de la Brigade mobile de contrôle économique et de la répression des fraudes (BMCRF), Sanibè Faho, a effectué le 11 août 2026 à Ouagadougou, une visite inopinée dans les usines de production de farine de blé, Moulin double star M2S de Gampéla et Moulin minor S.A. de Kossodo en vue de constater la disponibilité de la farine. Des rumeurs font état d’une rupture de la farine de blé causant ainsi la fermeture de certaines boulangeries et d’une possible augmentation du prix du pain. En vue d’édifier les consommateurs, une équipe de la Brigade mobile de contrôle économique et de la répression des fraudes (BMCRF), conduite par son coordonnateur, Sanibè Faho, a visité deux usines de production de la farine de blé ce 11 août 2026 à Ouaga-dougou. Il s’est agi du Moulin double star M2S de Gampéla et du Moulin minor S.A. de Kossodo. A Gampéla, dans le Moulin double star M2S, l’équipe a visité toute la chaine de production de la réception et le stockage du blé au conditionnement en passant par l’écrasement. Selon le directeur d’exploitation, Mahaz Zidnaba, actuellement l’usine possède un stock de 18 000 tonnes. « Aussi, on travaille 24 heures sur 24 pour une production de 300 tonnes par jour, soit 220 tonnes de farine et 80 tonnes de son. La farine de blé est disponible car chaque jour, on fait sortir environ 200 tonnes de farine à livrer à nos clients », a-t-il précisé. Même son de cloche au Moulin minor S.A. à Kossodo. Là, les machines tournent 24H/24 et pro-duisent 340 tonnes de farine de blé par jour. « On a eu certes quelques difficultés d’approvisionnement de la matière première dû au fret en début du mois d’août mais aujourd’hui tout est rentré dans l’ordre car nous avons un stock de 5 000 tonnes dans le silo. Il sera renforcé très bientôt par 30 000 tonnes de blé en provenance de Lomé (12 000T) et Abidjan (18 000T) », a expliqué le directeur de production de Moulin minor S.A. Bourahima Guigma. 800 tonnes de farine produites par jour Au regard de tout cela, Sanibè Faho s’est dit rassurer par rapport à la disponibilité de la farine de blé, mais aussi de la cadence de production où des équipes produisent 24 heures sur 24, avec une production qui tourne autour de 220 tonnes par jour dans le premier moulin et 340 tonnes par jour pour le 2e moulin. « Nous avons une production de 800 tonnes de farine de blé par jour. En principe, avec cette production et une répartition équitable faite à travers le réseau de chaînes de distribution, on ne devrait pas avoir de rupture de pain sur le marché », a-t-il constaté. Qu’à cela ne tienne, a poursuivi le coordonnateur de la BMCRF, les investigations vont se poursuivre pour éviter que les distributeurs auprès de ces deux moulins ne puissent pas spéculer sur les marchés. « Nous avons la liste de l’ensemble de ces clients, à leur tour aussi, ils vont nous expliquer le processus de répartition, soit au niveau des boulangeries ou de leur clientèle », a promis Sanibè Faho. Fleur BIRBA Aissatou DIARRA (Stagiaire)

items.title: Coopération sino-burkinabè : des journalistes et communicateurs en immersion en Chine
items.description: Une vingtaine de responsables de médias, de journalistes et de communicateurs du Burkina Faso prennent part du 8 au 27 août 2026 à Beijing, en République populaire de Chine, à un séminaire de formation. A l’issue de ce séjour, l’objectif des deux parties est d’approfondir la coopération sino-burkinabè dans le secteur des médias. La coopération entre la République populaire de Chine et le Burkina Faso est au beau fixe, depuis le rétablissement des relations diplomatiques entre les deux pays en 2018. Ils ne cessent depuis lors de renforcer leur partenariat dans divers secteurs et celui des médias n’est pas en reste. C’est à cet effet que 23 Burkinabè, composés de responsables de médias, de journalistes et communicateurs, ont été invités par le gouvernement de la République populaire de Chine à une session de formation du 8 au 27 août 2026 à Beijing. Lors de la cérémonie d’ouverture de ce séminaire de formation, le 8 août dernier, les organisateurs ont loué le développement constant des relations sino-burkinabè depuis leur rétablissement en 2018. « La confiance politique s’est renforcée, les résultats de la coopération ont augmenté et les échanges sont en plein essor, écrivant un nouveau chapitre de solidarité, de coopération gagnant-gagnant et d'amitié », a insisté le sous-directeur régional de l’Administration nationale de la radio et de la télévision, Yang Yong. Ainsi, lors de leur séjour de 21 jours en Chine, les hommes de médias burkinabè seront éclairés, à travers des conférences, sur des modules tels que « Politiques et situation de Chine ainsi que son développement dans le domaine des médias », « Impacts des technologies numériques sur les médias », « Technologies des nouveaux médias » et « coopération et pratique ». Lors de la conférence inaugurale, le sous-directeur régional de l’Administration nationale de la radio et de la télévision, Yang Yong, a indiqué que la Chine compte à ce jour 2 512 stations de radios et de télévisions dont 2 sont implantées au niveau central, 30 dans les provinces, 333 dans les villes et plus de 2000 dans les comtés. « Toutes ces stations sont publiques. Mais, il y a 3186 producteurs de l’audio-visuel en ligne dont la plupart sont des privés », a-t-il précisé. Comme dans la plupart des pays du monde, Yang Yong a reconnu qu’en Chine, les médias traditionnels éprouvent d’énormes difficultés face à l’émergence des nouveaux médias. Iqiyi, Tencent, Tiktok…ont en effet le vent en poupe. « Les médias traditionnels ont donc de moins en moins d’influence, de téléspectateurs et de recettes », a-t-il affirmer, tout en déclarant que ces médias ont été dans l’obligation d’enrichir leur contenu. Des défis communs Les défis sont énormes aussi bien pour les médias chinois que burkinabè, a souligné le directeur général adjoint de la China broadcasting international economic and techincal cooépartion (CBIC), He Dongbo. D’où selon lui, l’importance de ce séminaire de formation. « Nous estimons qu’à l’heure où la vague numérique transforme le monde, la coopération sino-burkinabè dans le secteur des médias ne se limite pas à un transfert de technologie, mais constitue un enrichissement mutuel de civilisation et une recherche de bénéfice partagé », a-t-il souhaité. Aussi, les journalistes et communicateurs burkinabè ne se contenteront pas seulement des panels et des débats dans les salles de conférence de Beijing durant tout leur séjour. Des visites de terrain sont prévues dans la province du Hunan, au Sud du pays. « Sur le terrain vous constaterez vous-même la vitalité innovante des technologies audiovisuelles chinoises et la richesse de notre patrimoine culturel révolutionnaire », a promis le directeur général de la CBIC aux séminaristes burkinabè. Il s’agit, a-t-il poursuivi, d’aider les journalistes et communicateurs burkinabè à appréhender l’importance du développement numérique et à tirer des enseignements utiles pour la transformation de leurs médias. « Nous sommes convaincus que c’est en apprenant les concepts dans les salles de conférence et en observant le développement sur le terrain que l’on peut vous aider à comprendre une vraie Chine multidimensionnelle et complète », a conclu He Dongbo. En attendant, les membres de la délégation burkinabè ont rallié lec 10 août Changsha, la capitale de la province du Hunan où ils ont entamé le lendemain la visite de terrain et, leur hôte promet leur en mettre plein les yeux sur le savoir-faire technologique chinois durant leur séjour de 5 jours dans la région natale de Mao-Zedong. Sié Simplice HIEN depuis Beijing

South Africa dump site collapse kills 14 suspected illegal miners
items.description: South African police have launched an investigation after 14 suspected illegal miners died when a mine dump site collapsed on them on Monday night. Eight others were injured and “an unknown number… may still be trapped underground”, police said in a statement. The site was being legally operated by a mining company and it is unclear how the miners, most of whom are believed to be from neighbouring Lesotho, gained access. Illegal mining is rife in South Africa as miners, known in South Africa as “zama zamas” (“those who try their luck” in Zulu), try to eke out a living by digging in abandoned shafts or dump sites. Regional police chief Lt-Gen Arthur Adams, who visited the scene on Tuesday morning, said that the dump site was being used to mine platinum and other metals by a local company. He told local broadcaster Newzroom Afrika that the “walls of the dumping site… caved in on them [the zama zamas]”. Adams said that three of the injured miners have since been released from hospital and have been detained by police. He confirmed that all the zama zamas are undocumented foreign nationals and will also face illegal mining and trespassing charges. Adams said the search continues for any miners who may still be trapped under the rubble. “As it stands, the excavation operations have ceased,” he said. Injuries and deaths of illegal miners are not uncommon in South Africa, especially at abandoned mine shafts. In January last year, 78 bodies were recovered from a disused shaft in Stilfontein , south-west of Johannesburg, The miners had been stuck there following a nationwide police operation to end illicit mining at disused sites that had closed, as the industry – once the backbone of the country’s economy – was shrinking. It is no longer profitable for mining multinationals to operate in many places, but the promise of still finding gold deposits proves was a magnet for many desperate people particularly undocumented migrants.

items.title: Musique traditionnelle : Koridjôme, la guitare birifor en voie de disparition
items.description: Longtemps perçu à tort comme un « instrument de malheur » au sein des communautés djan, dagara et birifor, le koridjôme est aujourd’hui en voie de disparition. La préservation de cette guitare traditionnelle à cordes représente un enjeu culturel majeur. A Loto, un village situé à quelques cinq kilomètres de Diébougou, dans la province de la Bougouriba, Dagnir Guekoumaté Dabiré, élevé au rang de Trésor humain vivant (THV), perpétue un double savoir-faire : la fabrication de l’instrument et l’art de la composition musicale. Il s’y investit corps et âme pour protéger et transmettre la mémoire musicale de son peuple. Assis sur un tabouret à trois pieds, Dagnir Guekoumaté Dabiré, 46 ans, procède en cette matinée du vendredi 26 juin 2026, à des essais sonores, appelés “pifou”. Puis, entonne en langue birifor un chant appelant à la cohésion sociale. « Jadis, la solidarité était le socle de notre société. Mes paroles invitent à renforcer l’entente entre les populations », explique-il. L’instrument de musique qu’il utilise est parfois orthographié koridjôme ou korindjom. C’est l’un des plus anciens instruments traditionnels des communautés djan, dagara et birifor, des groupes ethniques établis dans la région du Djôrô (Sud-Ouest du Burkina Faso). Cette guitare traditionnelle à sept cordes a subi pendant longtemps des préjugés. « A notre jeune âge, nous étions nombreux à y jouer. Certes beaucoup ne sont plus de ce monde aujourd’hui, mais à part moi, plus personne ne touche à cet instrument », confie Dagnir Guekoumaté Dabiré. Pour l’octogénaire, Palenfo Tiarkoun, «le koridjôme conseille, il n’est pas fait pour le mal ». La raison de ce désamour ? Des croyances qui lui collent une étiquette de jeteur de sort. L’artiste-musicien évoque le cas d’un ami proche, doté d’une oreille musicale parfaite, que son grand frère a obligé à abandonner la musique. Pour lui : « jouer du koridjôme était porteur de mauvaise fortune. Il ressassait des rumeurs affirmant que le joueur de koridjôme ne pourrait jamais avoir d’enfant. Pourtant, j’ai des enfants et j’ai essayé en vain de le raisonner. Il n’a rien voulu entendre », regrette le musicien, le regard empreint d’amertume. A ses côtés, Palenfo Tiarkoun (83 ans), écoute la conversation avec attention. Ses cheveux blancs et ses traits marqués témoignent d’une vie entière imprégnée de culture locale. Elle s’empresse de corroborer les propos du musicien. « Je connais bien le koridjôme. En plus du balafon, nos parents avaient fait de cette guitare, le principal instrument de notre identité culturelle. J’ai aussi entendu ces rumeurs de malédiction. Mais l’expérience m’a prouvé qu’un malfaiteur qui écoute le koridjôme peut changer de comportement. Cet instrument conseille. Il n’est pas fait pour le mal. Dieu nous a donné notre fils Dagnir Guekoumaté. Le directeur provincial chargé de la culture de la Bougouriba, Abdoul Aziz Bationo, rappelle que le koridjôme requiert un savoir-faire technique très précis. " data-large-file="https://www.sidwaya.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Ph4-1024x768.jpg" class="size-medium wp-image-167441" src="https://www.sidwaya.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Ph4-300x225.jpg" alt="" width="300" height="225" srcset="https://www.sidwaya.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Ph4-300x225.jpg 300w, https://www.sidwaya.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Ph4-1024x768.jpg 1024w, https://www.sidwaya.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Ph4-768x576.jpg 768w, https://www.sidwaya.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Ph4-1536x1152.jpg 1536w, https://www.sidwaya.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Ph4-560x420.jpg 560w, https://www.sidwaya.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Ph4-80x60.jpg 80w, https://www.sidwaya.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Ph4-150x112.jpg 150w, https://www.sidwaya.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Ph4-696x522.jpg 696w, https://www.sidwaya.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Ph4-1068x801.jpg 1068w, https://www.sidwaya.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Ph4-265x198.jpg 265w, https://www.sidwaya.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Ph4.jpg 1575w" sizes="(max-width: 300px) 100vw, 300px" /> Le directeur provincial chargé de la culture de la Bougouriba, Abdoul Aziz Bationo, rappelle que le koridjôme requiert un savoir-faire technique très précis. Il nous fait honneur en perpétuant notre tradition», clame-t-elle. Pour composer ses mélodies sur sept notes, Dagnir Guekoumaté Dabiré dit s’en remettre à une inspiration mystique. « Je n’ai jamais appris à chanter. Les chansons me viennent en rêve. Je me réveille, je les répète. Il en est de même pour l’assemblage de la guitare. A la suite d’un songe, je me suis rendu en brousse après avoir demandé la permission aux mânes et aux ancêtres. J’ai coupé des branches de l’arbre (ndlr: l’ébénier d’Afrique), que j’ai courbées à la maison pour former un demi-cercle, avant de les fixer à une calebasse bien taillée », relate-t-il. Un savoir-faire ancestral transmis oralement Selon le directeur provincial de la communication, de la culture, des arts et du tourisme de la Bougouriba, Abdoul Aziz Bationo, la fabrication du koridjôme obéit à un rituel technique très précis. Ses recherches sur le terrain confirment ce processus rigoureux. « Il faut d’abord couper une branche de l’ébénier d’Afrique avec l’assentiment des esprits de la brousse. Ensuite, on l’assouplit à l’aide d’une fourche d’arbre pour la plier en forme de manche. On la laisse sécher pendant un mois, puis on sculpte l’extrémité et on y perce sept trous », explique-t-il. La préparation de la caisse de résonance exige tout autant de rigueur. « Il faut un vrai savoir-faire agricole pour sélectionner une calebasse mûre et de bonne qualité. « Les chansons me viennent en rêve. Il en est de même pour l’assemblage de la guitare », affirme l’artiste Dagnir Guekoumaté Dabiré. " data-large-file="https://www.sidwaya.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Ph2-2-1024x581.jpg" class="size-medium wp-image-167439" src="https://www.sidwaya.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Ph2-2-300x170.jpg" alt="" width="300" height="170" srcset="https://www.sidwaya.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Ph2-2-300x170.jpg 300w, https://www.sidwaya.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Ph2-2-1024x581.jpg 1024w, https://www.sidwaya.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Ph2-2-768x435.jpg 768w, https://www.sidwaya.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Ph2-2-1536x871.jpg 1536w, https://www.sidwaya.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Ph2-2-741x420.jpg 741w, https://www.sidwaya.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Ph2-2-150x85.jpg 150w, https://www.sidwaya.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Ph2-2-696x395.jpg 696w, https://www.sidwaya.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Ph2-2-1068x606.jpg 1068w, https://www.sidwaya.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Ph2-2.jpg 1575w" sizes="(max-width: 300px) 100vw, 300px" /> « Les chansons me viennent en rêve. Il en est de même pour l’assemblage de la guitare », affirme l’artiste Dagnir Guekoumaté Dabiré. On l’évide, découpe sa partie supérieure, puis on y perce cinq trous pour y insérer le manche. Le tout est fixé à l’aide de caoutchouc et de fibres d’oseille. Enfin, on façonne sept rondelles de calebasse qui servent d’accordeurs. On insère les fils de nylon et on ajuste les cordes », précise M. Bationo. Face au risque d’extinction de ce patrimoine, le directeur provincial rassure : « le gouvernement, à travers le ministère de la Culture, a élevé Dagnir Guekoumaté Dabiré au rang de Trésor humain vivant pour l’encourager à valoriser cet instrument et à transmettre son art à la jeunesse. Nous l’intégrons déjà dans les événements culturels provinciaux et régionaux. Notre ambition est de le faire intervenir en milieu scolaire dans les années à venir, à l’occasion du mois artistique et culturel », annonce-t-il. La relève s’organise à Loto Dagnir Guekoumaté Dabiré refuse de voir son art s’éteindre. «Je ne peux pas arrêter de Ollo Kambiré (gauche) et Sié Kambiré (droite) s’engagent désormais à faire vivre la culture birifor à travers le koridjôme. " data-large-file="https://www.sidwaya.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Ph6-1024x581.jpg" class="size-medium wp-image-167443" src="https://www.sidwaya.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Ph6-300x170.jpg" alt="" width="300" height="170" srcset="https://www.sidwaya.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Ph6-300x170.jpg 300w, https://www.sidwaya.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Ph6-1024x581.jpg 1024w, https://www.sidwaya.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Ph6-768x435.jpg 768w, https://www.sidwaya.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Ph6-1536x871.jpg 1536w, https://www.sidwaya.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Ph6-741x420.jpg 741w, https://www.sidwaya.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Ph6-150x85.jpg 150w, https://www.sidwaya.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Ph6-696x395.jpg 696w, https://www.sidwaya.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Ph6-1068x606.jpg 1068w, https://www.sidwaya.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Ph6.jpg 1575w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 300px) 100vw, 300px" /> Ollo Kambiré (gauche) et Sié Kambiré (droite) s’engagent désormais à faire vivre la culture birifor à travers le koridjôme. jouer. C’est un don de Dieu », confie-t-il. Heureusement, son cri du cœur résonne auprès de la jeune génération de Loto. Son propre fils, Anamala Frédéric Dabiré, en classe de 4e au Collège d’enseignement général (CEG) de Loto, s’est initié à la guitare birifor dès 2018. Aujourd’hui, il accompagne fièrement son père lors des cérémonies officielles. « Quand je joue du koridjôme, cela me procure une immense joie. Je n’abandonnerai jamais cet instrument légué par nos ancêtres. Nous avons le devoir de le protéger », estime-t-il. Même enthousiasme chez Dominique Kambiré, élève en classe de 3e. « Nous jouons ensemble chaque soir après les cours et les week-ends », se réjouit-il. Si ces deux adolescents sont désormais les compagnons de l’artiste lors de ses prestations, d’autres adultes franchissent le pas. Ollo Kambiré, 40 ans, empoigne l’instrument avec humilité. Les jeunes apprenants, Anamala Frédéric Dabiré et Dominique Kambiré, en pleine répétition aux côtés de leur maître. Mais je vais faire des efforts pour apprendre. C’est un devoir », se résout M. Dabiré. Plus jeune, Sié Kambiré, 25 ans, se souvient avec nostalgie de son enfance rythmée par ces mélodies : « Il n’est pas trop tard pour apprendre. Nous allons travailler pour faire revivre la culture birifor ». Ces marques d’intérêt sont une immense victoire pour Dagnir Guekoumaté Dabiré. L’artiste, qui a produit en 2021 un album de dix titres (huit en Birifor et deux en Dioula), espère trouver des soutiens pour enregistrer de nouveaux projets. En attendant, il met sa notoriété au service de la communauté en animant chaque semaine l’émission intitulé “Barodéni”, sur les ondes de la radio catholique “UNITAS” de Diébougou. Un rendez-vous de deux heures durant lequel, il dispense des conseils sur le vivre-ensemble et la vie de couple. Karim DIANDA Dagnir Guekoumaté Dabiré élevé au rang de Trésor humain vivant Reconnu pour sa maîtrise parfaite du koridjôme, Dagnir Guekoumaté Dabiré, résidant à Loto, a été officiellement élevé au rang de Trésor humain vivant(THV) dans le domaine de l’artisanat traditionnel. Cette prestigieuse distinction lui a été décernée le 17 avril 2026 à Ouahigouya, lors du lancement officiel du Mois du patrimoine. En reconnaissance de son action en faveur de la préservation et de la transmission culturelle, il a également été fait Chevalier de l’Ordre de l’Etalon. Cette double distinction consacre un parcours dédié à la valorisation des savoir-faire traditionnels et invite à la promotion du patrimoine culturel burkinabè. Sourire aux lèvres, ce filiforme est l’aîné d’une fratrie de 10 enfants. On le reconnaît aisément à la croix de cauris qu’il arbore fièrement. « J’ai vu cette croix ainsi que mon sac en songe, et je les ai fabriqués à mon réveil », raconte-t-il. Son parcours est profondément ancré dans la tradition : son prénom “Guekouma” signifie “faire souffrir pour tuer”, tandis que le suffixe “té” atteste de son initiation selon le rite du rameau lobi. Né le jour de l’implantation du fétiche birifor éponyme, il porte fièrement le nom de “Dagnir”. K.D.

items.title: Thailand suspends new gun permits after mass shooting
items.description: Thailand’s government will immediately stop issuing gun permits after a shooting incident last week in which a 14-year-old killed eight people and himself. Existing gun owners are already banned from carrying their weapons in public. The South East Asian country has one of the highest rates of civilian gun ownership in the region, with around 10.3 million firearms in civilian possession, and high levels of gun crime. In response to the recent shooting, the prime minister has promised to pass tough new gun control laws with severe penalties, suspending new permits in the meantime. Last Friday, a pupil at Debsirin Nonthaburi School outside Bangkok shot his grandparents using a handgun owned by his grandfather, before opening fire at teachers and students at school, authorities say. Both grandparents, five staff members at the school and one 12-year-old girl died. Police believe the shooter may have taught himself to use a gun via social media. They say there is evidence that the boy watched violent content online, and that he showed a strong interest in learning how to handle guns. His consumption of this content as well as anxiety over studies and family issues might have also fuelled his actions, they add. Officials paid their respects to the victims on Tuesday at a Nonthaburi temple Until further notice, no new permits to purchase or own guns will be issued. Existing purchase permits will not be renewed but it is unclear what will happen to existing gun ownership permits. Permits to carry guns were suspended in late 2023 – owners must keep their weapons at home or at a shooting range. The government is also considering measures to persuade the owners of an estimated four million unlicensed guns to hand them over in the wake of the school shooting. Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul has said the announced measures will remain in place as the government works to pass new gun control laws, with stronger controls and significantly harsher penalties. Gun control advocates have called for mental health assessments as part of the permit process, and for permits to be periodically re-evaluated. Anutin has said stricter ammunition controls are in his sights, while the education minister has proposed screening at the entrance of schools to stop students from bringing in weapons.

Accord technique entre la Guinée et le FMI : « Les 425 millions de dollars doivent être considérés comme un levier plutôt que comme une solution » (ministre)
items.description: Le gouvernement de la République de Guinée, à travers le ministère de l’Économie, des Finances et du Budget, le ministère du Plan et de la Coopération internationale ainsi que la Banque centrale de la République de Guinée (BCRG), a tenu, ce mardi 11 août 2026, un point de presse pour expliquer les tenants et aboutissants de la conclusion d’un accord technique avec les services du Fonds monétaire international (FMI). Cet accord porte sur la mise en place d’un nouveau programme économique et financier de 41 mois, soutenu par la Facilité élargie de crédit (FEC), pour un financement de près de 425 millions de dollars. Selon le gouvernement, cet accord devrait permettre à la République de Guinée de consolider la stabilité macroéconomique et d’accompagner sa transformation économique. Dans sa prise de parole, la ministre de l’Économie, des Finances et du Budget, Mariama Ciré Camara, a déclaré : « Les 425 millions de dollars du FMI doivent être considérés comme un levier plutôt que comme une solution. Le financement peut accompagner les réformes, renforcer la crédibilité économique du pays et soutenir les besoins de financement. Il ne remplacera toutefois pas la nécessité d’améliorer la mobilisation des recettes, la qualité de la dépense publique et l’efficacité des institutions. » Le prochain test sera donc celui de l’exécution, a-t-elle indiqué : « La Guinée devra démontrer qu’elle peut transformer ses ambitions en résultats mesurables : davantage de recettes internes, une meilleure gestion budgétaire, des investissements plus productifs, une économie plus diversifiée et surtout davantage d’emplois et de services publics pour les citoyens. » En définitive, a-t-elle assuré, « l’enjeu du nouvel accord avec le FMI dépasse largement les 425 millions de dollars. Il s’agit pour la Guinée de profiter d’une période exceptionnelle de croissance et d’investissements pour poser les bases d’un modèle économique moins dépendant des ressources extractives et davantage capable de financer son propre développement. » De son côté, le ministre du Plan et de la Coopération internationale, Ismaël Nabé, estime que cet accord renforce la crédibilité de la Guinée auprès de ses partenaires. « Cet accord donne une signature et une crédibilité à la Guinée. Nous avons un plan ambitieux de développement qui est le programme Simandou 2040. La Guinée doit mobiliser plus de 300 et quelques poussières de milliards de dollars pour les 15 prochaines années pour financer les projets. Ces projets sont divers. Quand vous prenez les cinq piliers, en faisant un investissement dans l’agriculture et l’agro-industrie, ça peut créer de l’emploi. Mais aussi l’éducation et la culture », a-t-il expliqué. Poursuivant, le ministre a souligné que « plus de 10 projets structurants doivent être exécutés au cours des cinq prochaines années », notamment dans les secteurs de l’éducation et de la santé publique. Concernant les infrastructures, Ismaël Nabé a indiqué que « 15 projets doivent être développés », notamment dans les domaines des routes, des pistes rurales, des ports et des aéroports. Pour sa part, le gouverneur de la BCRG, Dr Karamo Kaba, a insisté sur l’importance de la crédibilité que cet accord pourrait apporter à la politique économique du pays. « La valeur de cet accord ne se résume pas seulement en dollars ou en francs guinéens. Sa véritable valeur réside dans la crédibilité qu’il apporte à notre politique économique, dans la confiance qu’il peut susciter auprès des investisseurs et de nos partenaires. Après une croissance estimée à 6,9 % en 2025, notre économie devrait progresser d’environ 8,8 % en 2026 et d’environ 10 % entre 2027 et 2030, notamment grâce au secteur minier et à la montée en puissance de Simandou », a affirmé le patron de la BCRG. Elisa Camara & Ousmane Camara L’article Accord technique entre la Guinée et le FMI : « Les 425 millions de dollars doivent être considérés comme un levier plutôt que comme une solution » (ministre) est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Musique : David le Combattant présente son nouvel album « Dounia ya sougri »
items.description: L’artiste chanteur, Harouna David Malgoubri, dit David Le Combattant, a officiellement présenté son nouvel album, intitulé : « Dounia ya sougri », le dimanche 9 août 2026 à l’espace culturel de Koupéla. La cérémonie de dédicace du nouvel album intitulé : « Dounia ya sougri », de l’artiste chanteur, Harouna David Malgoubri, dit David Le Combattant, a débuté par la présentation de nouveaux morceaux et la diffusion du nouveau. Composé de neuf titres, cet opus a été dévoilé aux hommes et femmes des médias ainsi qu’aux mélomanes, en présence des parents, amis, connaissances et de nombreux fans venus apporter leur soutien à l’artiste, le dimanche 9 août 2026 à l’espace culturel de Koupéla. Après la présentation, l’artiste a ensuite pris possession de la scène pour offrir un véritable show au public. A travers ses prestations, il a démontré une fois de plus son engagement à contribuer au développement et à la promotion de la culture burkinabè. Pour David Le Combattant, « Dounia ya sougri », qui signifie littéralement « le monde, c’est le pardon », est un album porteur d’un message d’espoir, de pardon et de paix. « A travers cet album, je veux inviter chacun à pardonner et à garder espoir. Malgré les difficultés que traverse notre société, nous devons continuer à croire en un avenir meilleur et travailler pour la paix et la cohésion entre les filles et fils du Burkina Faso », a-t-il expliqué. L’artiste a également dédié cet opus aux combattants ainsi qu’à tous les révolutionnaires burkinabè. Selon lui, leur engagement et leur sacrifice doivent servir d’exemple à la jeune génération. « Je dédie cet album à tous nos combattants et à tous ceux qui se battent pour le Burkina. Nous devons rester unis et déterminés. Je crois que la paix n’est plus loin. Mais, elle nécessite l’engagement et la solidarité de tous », a-t-il déclaré. Du côté des fans, la satisfaction était également au rendez-vous. Justin Silga, admirateur de l’artiste, n’a pas manqué de saluer cette nouvelle production. « Je le félicite pour ce nouvel album. Nous avons découvert de belles chansons et un artiste toujours engagé. Je l’encourage à continuer dans cette dynamique et nous, les fans, allons l’accompagner pour que son œuvre puisse aller encore plus loin », a-t-il confié. Ce concert-dédicace a ainsi offert aux mélomanes l’occasion de revivre la performance scénique de David Le Combattant et de découvrir les différentes sonorités de son nouvel album. Entre musique, messages de paix et communion avec le public, l’artiste a voulu faire de cette sortie discographique un moment de partage et de célébration de la culture burkinabè. Disponible désormais sur le marché, « Dounia ya sougri » est vendu sur clé USB au prix de 10 000 F CFA l’unité. Les fans et mélomanes sont donc invités à se procurer l’album afin de soutenir l’artiste et de contribuer à la promotion de la musique burkinabè. Amedée SILGA

items.title: La nature se révolte
items.description: Inondations aux effets dévastateurs et incendies du même calibre, la planète Terre dans sa globalité ressent de plus en plus les effets des changements climatiques avec à la clé un réchauffement planétaire excessif et la nécessité d’une prise de conscience urgente et absolue pour prévenir la catastrophe majeure qui se dessine, à savoir la disparition pure et simple de la planète terre. Ce n’est pas tomber dans l’exagération que de le dire, car, la course à l’industrialisation et l’utilisation massive des énergies fossiles qui en découle, la reprise des programmes de réarmement militaire des grandes puissances, la déforestation des principaux poumons de la planète à savoir la forêt d’Amazonie et celle équatorienne, ont mis notre habitat commun dans l’orange, et, la tendance n’est pas près de s’inverser au vu des crises multiples et multiformes qui secouent la planète. Face à cette folie humaine, des pays refusent la fatalité en privilégiant la transition écologique dans le domaine de l’habitat et en supprimant les nuisances à un environnement sain. Vivre dans un environnement bienveillant soucieux de la préservation de la nature voilà le credo. Il s’agit donc, d’inventer la ville de demain à travers de grandes opérations d’urbanisme qui offrent un nouveau type d’habitat vert et ouvert sur l’environnement. Par ailleurs, de vastes campagnes de reforestation sont entreprises chaque année avec le souci évident de stopper l’avancée du désert. Construire, protéger, rénover, assainir. Bref, mettre l’écologie au service du développement durable et du bien-être des masses populaires. Hélas, les prédateurs sont eux aussi à la tâche avec les milieux ultralibéraux dont le seul leitmotiv demeure le profit. On retrouve ici la contradiction principale et la mère de toutes les batailles qui ont secoué l’humanité, à savoir l’opposition entre l’homme et le capital. Ou plutôt entre les intérêts des deux. Pour l’heure, la planète gronde ! Boubakar SY
